anomalies.observed: On the Microcontroller sheet the global label NET0009 is attached simultaneously to the USB-C D- pins (J6 A7/B7), to the ESP32-C3 USB_D-/GPIO18 pin (U4 pin 26), and to the data input DIN of the WS2812B status LED (D5 pin 1). Thus the USB D- line and the NeoPixel data line are merged onto one net.
anomalies.expected: USB D- must connect only to the ESP32-C3 native-USB peripheral pin (GPIO18/USB_D-); the WS2812B DIN must be on its own dedicated GPIO net so the status LED can be driven independently of the USB programming link. The spec describes USB-C as the 'logic/programming supply' and the WS2812B as a separate status LED, which cannot share the USB D- net.

evidence.quote: mcu.kicad_sch: J6 USB_C_Receptacle A7/B7 (D-) -> NET0009; U4 GPIO18/USB_D- (pin 26) -> NET0009; D5 WS2812B DIN -> NET0009
Accepts power from either a 12 V barrel jack ... or USB-C 5 V (J12, logic/programming supply) ... Exposes status over Wi-Fi ... and a single onboard WS2812B status LED (D1).

anomalies.impact: The USB D- data line is shorted to the WS2812B data input. USB programming/communication would be corrupted by the LED's data line (and its pull/decoupling), and the status LED would receive USB traffic instead of the MCU's LED data, so neither the USB interface nor the status LED behaves as intended.

parsed.summary: The power, thermocouple-SPI, heater-switch and buck sections match the specification (allowing for the build's renumbered references), but on the MCU sheet the global net NET0009 bridges the USB-C D- line / ESP32 GPIO18-USB_D- to the WS2812B status-LED DIN, merging two unrelated signals and breaking both USB programming and LED control.
